page.layout: Running head at top centre ("PARS PRIMA.") and page number at top right ("133"). Two medallion portraits with legends side by side at the top, full width. One column of text below them, two paragraphs. Signature "Kk 3" at the bottom right of the text block. No marginal notes.

main_text.l: LAG.F.R.AEG. PTOLOMEVS
BERONICE[?] PTOLOM.
PTOLEMAEVS Lagi filius, mortuo Alexandro Ma-
gno, ab equitibus primùm, deinde communi omnium consen-
su Ægypti rex declaratur, anno mundi 3640. ante Christum
natum 322.huic Africæ, Arabiæque pars cum Aegypto forte
venit: ex gregario milite eum Alexander virtutis causa eve-
xerat. In Ægypto folerti industria magnas opes paravit: Ægy-
ptios insigni moderatione in favorem sui solicitavit, & reges
finitimos obsequiis devinxit: terminos imperij, urbe Cyrene
ampliavit:tantúsq; factus est, ut non tam hostes timeret, quàm
timendus ipse hostibus esset. Demetrium Antigoni filium bel-
lo vicit:captiuos,omnémq; prædam dimisit: se propter digni-
tatem,non propter prædam pugnasse dictitans. Posthæc victor
ipse à victo navali prælio vincitur: filium & fratrem atque
amicos Ptolemæi captos, Demetrius pari antea munere pro-
vocatus, in Ægyptum remittit: donísque inter ipsa bella con-
tendunt:tanto honestius tunc bella gerebantur, quanto nunc
amicitiæ coluntur. Vide Justin.lib.13.14.&15. Legatos ex Ale-
xandria misit Romam conciliandæ amicitiæ gratia: imperavit
annis 40. Cyprum & Phoeniciam tenuit: ab hoc omnes alij re-
ges Ægyptiaci, vocati sunt Ptolemæi.
BERENICE uxor fuit Ptolemæi prædicti, de cuius no-
mine Philadelphus eius filius, quam in sinu Arabico extruxit
urbem, appellavit. Fuit & altera Berenice, Philadelphi & Arsi-
noes filia, quæ Ptolemæo Euergeti nupsit, cuius crines in cœ-
lum relati feruntur, autore Conone mathematico.

page.notes: Medallion legends are transcribed as lines; the curved lettering of the right medallion ("BERONICE") is only partly certain. The 1-2 forms "3 6 4 o." and "3 2 2" are read as 3640 and 322. Spelling "Justin" follows the rule for i/j, the printed form is "Iustin". No marginal notes or catchword on this page.
